```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", eval = FALSE)
```

`new_table_block()` shows the data it receives as an interactive table and
passes the data on, filtered by the reader's last click if `drill` is set.
`layout` decides what a row is; `look` how it is drawn.

```{r}
library(blockr.core)
library(blockr.viz)

serve(new_table_block(), data = list(data = iris))
```

## Records

The default layout shows the input's rows, with search and sort.

```{r}
new_table_block(rowname = "name", columns = c("mpg", "hp", "wt"))

# rows under one collapsible header per cylinder count
new_table_block(by = "cyl", columns = c("mpg", "hp"))
```

`shadings` colors cells: `"diverging"` centers on zero, `"sequential"`
ramps two colors, `"bar"` draws a data bar.

```{r}
new_table_block(shadings = list(
  list(mode = "bar", columns = c("mpg", "hp")),
  list(mode = "diverging", columns = "change", domain = c(-1, 1))
))
```

A finished table from R code, such as a structured or annotated data frame
(`as_annotated_df()`), is drawn as it comes.

## Groups

One row per level of `by`, one column per entry of `summaries`. Each entry
is a list with a `type` and that type's keys:

| type | a column of |
|---|---|
| `"simple"` | a count or statistic, as a number, bar, dot or tile |
| `"dist"` | a box, point range or text of a column's spread |
| `"field"` | the distinct values of a column |
| `"sparkline"` | a small line of a column over `x` |
| `"spans"` | intervals from `x` to `xend` on a time line |
| `"pair"` | two points per row, from `x` to `xend` |
| `"expr"` | an R expression evaluated per row group |
| `"custom"` | a function of the row group's rows |

```{r}
new_table_block(
  layout = "groups", by = "Species",
  summaries = list(
    list(type = "simple", func = "count"),
    list(type = "simple", func = "mean", col = "Sepal.Length",
         show = "number"),
    list(type = "dist", col = "Petal.Length", summary = "median_q1_q3",
         show = "box"),
    list(type = "expr", name = "Widest", expr = "max(Sepal.Width)")
  ),
  sort_by = "value", top_n = 10
)
```

`percent_of` sets the base of a count's percentage, `missing` keeps or drops
rows whose group is missing, and `top_n` folds the rows past the cut into
one "Other" row. `?new_table_block` lists every key of every type.

## Variables

A Table 1: one row per statistic or level of each variable, one column per
level of `by`.

```{r}
new_table_block(
  layout = "variables", by = "TRT01A",
  stats = c("n", "mean_sd", "median_q1_q3"),
  total = TRUE, id = "USUBJID"
)
```

## Looks

`look = "compact"` rotates the column titles and draws `tile` summaries as a
heatmap; `look = "cards"` draws one card per summary.

```{r}
new_table_block(
  layout = "groups", look = "cards",
  summaries = list(
    list(type = "simple", name = "Rows", func = "count"),
    list(type = "simple", func = "mean", col = "mpg")
  )
)
```

## Clicks

With `drill`, a click on a row filters the block's output. In records it
names the column to filter on, or `"auto"`; in groups and variables
`"auto"` filters on the clicked row's groups.

```{r}
new_table_block(layout = "groups", by = "region",
                summaries = list(list(type = "simple", func = "count")),
                drill = "auto")
```

## Downloads

With `download = TRUE` (the default) the block offers Excel (the values,
with their number format), a web page and PowerPoint, and an image where the
table draws marks.
